senses.gloss:
lājahoma
(‘offering parched grains into the fire’)
------------------------------------------
The धर्मशास्त्रस् or Hindu Lawbooks have prescribed sixteen सṁस्कारस् or sacraments for every human being, especially of the first three castes. Out of these विवाह or मर्रिअगे is a very important one.
Of the several steps involved in this saṁskāra, लाजहोम also is one.
The brother of the bride fills her joined palms with lāja or parched grains, mixed with शमी leaves (Prosopsis spicigera). She has to offer it into the consecrated fire while going round it. Her husband may touch her hands while she is offering.
The mantras uttered during this ceremony are addressed to the Vedic gods like वरुण and पूषन्, requesting them to loosen the bonds with her ड़थेर्, and strengthen the same towards her husband.
